lines.trans: This cigarette already tastes bitter.
Just throw it out quickly into the trash bin.
All right, I want to go to the bathroom.
Wait, it is on fire over there, friends!
The neighboring restaurant is burning right now!
Are you sure that this is a real fire?
Of course, look at this black smoke.
People are running out of the building onto the street.
We urgently need to tell the boss about this.
Yes, he must know about this fire.
Drop the cigarette and let's go inside faster.
I am running after you, open the door.

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: бегу, бежишь, ..., бегут

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.
Don't hang up!

examples.text: Он всегда бросает вещи на пол.
examples.trans: He always throws things on the floor.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.trans: Faster!
He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!
How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: не в моём вкусе = not my type
не в моём вкусе = not my type

examples.trans: You are not my type.
She has good taste.

examples.text: Я бы рад вам помочь. Но вы, к сожалению, не в моём вкусе.
examples.trans: I would be glad to help you. But unfortunately you are not my type.
We go inside quickly.
He looked inside the building.
Excellent. We go inside quickly.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'бегать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to run out'.

examples.text: Люди выбегают из здания на улицу.
examples.trans: People are running out of the building onto the street.

examples.text: Это слово «выбегать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to run out' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: выбросить в окно = to throw out the window

examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window.
Throw out this old rubbish.

examples.text: Он мэра в окно выбросил. Вы помните?
examples.trans: He threw the mayor out the window. Do you remember?

meanings.en: to burn, to be on fire, to glow
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to burn, to shine', paired with 'сгореть'.

examples.trans: The little flame is burning, but there is hardly any warmth.

examples.text: Только нашего русского размаха не хватает. Огонёк горит, а тепла мало.
examples.trans: Only it lacks our broad Russian scale. The little flame is burning, but there is hardly any warmth.

examples.text: У тебя на плите всё мясо горит!
examples.trans: All the meat on your stove is burning!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to taste bitter'.

examples.text: Эта сигарета уже горчит на вкус.
examples.trans: This cigarette already tastes bitter.

examples.text: Это слово «горчить» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to taste bitter' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'door' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Open the door.
The door is behind the wardrobe.
Open the door. Is this flat nine?

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)

examples.trans: I have to work.
Greed should be moderate.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.
He's my friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'smoke' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Smoke all around.

examples.text: Где мы? Кругом дым и воронки.
examples.trans: Where are we? Smoke and bomb craters are all around.

examples.text: Какой кошмар, на кухне полный дым!
examples.trans: What a nightmare, complete smoke in the kitchen!
Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: large structure such as an office, school, or hall

examples.text: На огромной скорости машина врезалась в здание!
examples.trans: At huge speed the car crashed into the building!
This is an old, beautiful building.

examples.text: Пятнадцать лет мы просим новое здание!
examples.trans: For fifteen years we've been asking for a new building!
As you all know...
I don't know.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'из мэрии' = from the town hall

examples.trans: The town hall called me.
He's from Moscow.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, я уже знаю. Мне звонили из мэрии.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.
Of course I'll help.
Yes, of course.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?
All right, here you go.
OK, I'm coming.
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary

examples.trans: It needs a wash.
We need to do even more.
It needs a wash!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.trans: This is real success!
He is a true friend.

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.
I open return fire!

examples.text: Внимательно проследи за огнём на сковороде.
examples.trans: Keep close watch on the fire on the skillet.

examples.text: Срочно снимай сковороду с горячего огня!
examples.trans: Urgently take the pan off the hot fire!

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

examples.trans: Grab him!
It needs a wash.
Four-eyes! Grab him!
She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: a door, window, bottle, or business

examples.trans: I'm going to open it now.
They open the shop at nine.
I am opening return fire!
Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: начался пожар = a fire broke out

examples.trans: A fire started there!
The firefighters quickly put out the fire.

examples.text: Там начался пожар! Везде пожарные машины и полиция!
examples.trans: A fire started there! Fire engines and police are everywhere!
May I go?
Let's go home.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look

examples.trans: May I have a look?
I only had a look.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: takes the accusative; everyday synonym of о

examples.trans: He says nasty things about me.
She knows everything about everyone.

examples.text: Как интересно! А в Москве ты про меня гадости рассказываешь.
examples.trans: How interesting! And in Moscow you go around saying nasty things about me.
Just like that?
Go straight along this street.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.
I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?
Drop the cigarette!
He smoked a cigarette.
Drop the cigarette! Smoking is very harmful!

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: comparative of скоро used as adverb or particle

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!
Rather yes than no.
Bring the clothespin quickly!

examples.text: За соседним столиком сидели приятные люди.
examples.trans: Pleasant people were sitting at the next table.
To a guest at the next table.

examples.text: В соседнем зале играет тихая музыка.
examples.trans: Quiet music plays in the neighboring hall.

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent!
I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: там такие деньги = there's so much money in it

examples.trans: Everything's fine there.
Who's there?
Hello! How was it in Hungary?
Where's the toilet?
The toilet is in the corridor.
Do you remember the toilet in the communal flat?

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный.
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident.
He answered in a calm, confident voice.

examples.text: Что-то голос какой-то не очень уверенный. Что конкретно?
examples.trans: Your voice doesn't sound very confident. What specifically?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: на улице = out on the street / outside
на улице холодно = it's cold outside

examples.text: На Московской улице перевернули ящики с мусором.
examples.trans: On Moskovskaya Street someone tipped over the rubbish bins.
We met on the street.
There are reporters out on the street!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'trash bin, urn' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да выбрось её скорее в урну.
examples.trans: Just throw it out quickly into the trash bin.

examples.text: Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
examples.trans: All by the rules, like a knights' tournament.
I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.
What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('black').

examples.trans: Listen, look in the black cabinet.

examples.text: На нём был строгий чёрный костюм.
examples.trans: He was wearing a formal black suit.

examples.text: Как не нашла? Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри. Там справа от двери!
examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't find it? Listen, look in the black cabinet. There to the right of the door!
Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
